Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec08HOhHaCjKLcrN.Bio: Matt Landman is an activist and filmmaker known for FrankenSkies, his documentary on geoengineering and chemtrails, and for organizing events such as the 2018 Global Summit to Stop Geoengineering. On InnerVerse he has discussed chemtrail activism, questioned the official COVID-19 narrative and mask mandates, and explored the West Coast fires.
rec08HOhHaCjKLcrN.Name: Matt Landman

rec0QPYzm6s8Y3CTq.Bio: Dylan Saccoccio is the author of the Spirit Whirled series, The Real Universal Empire, and the Tale of Onora. After chasing language back as far as possible, he now explores other avenues to prove cultural diffusion of the ancient universal empire of priests, navigators, masons, and merchants. Find his latest of many hundreds of articles on Substack.
rec0QPYzm6s8Y3CTq.Name: Dylan Saccoccio
rec0QPYzm6s8Y3CTq.Role: Author, & Researcher of Philology, History, & the Occult

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Truth Known by What It Is Not", "body": "Chance opens with the idea that truth, like freedom, is understood negatively: you could never list everything it is, only delete what it is not, the way natural law leaves countless rights and only a few wrongs. Dylan answers that the truth simply is, whatever our perceptions of it, and traces his framing to the Hermetic tradition of Hermes, Thoth and Mercury and to Mark Passio's natural law podcasts, arguing that wrong behavior programs slavery while right behavior programs freedom. Matt reads a Spirit Whirled passage on polarity, in which every paradox is unified once truth is treated as absolute."}, {"title": "Symbolic Literacy as Psychic Self-Defense", "body": "Chance argues that pairing Mark Passio's teaching on manipulation with the symbolic literacy in Dylan's work gives a listener a black belt in psychic self-defense, like putting on the truth glasses from They Live. Dylan says ancient allegory encoded survival knowledge in sun and Saturn imagery, and that recognizing it makes a person unhexable; he reads the name corona as crown symbolism running back to Kronos, the cube of the Kaaba and Solomon's seal. Matt holds up a San Francisco Chronicle front page and, in his reading, finds a long spell, a demon and the pandemic packed into one headline seen by millions."}, {"title": "Matt's Traveling Truth Box Library", "body": "Matt describes turning a neighborhood book box idea into a traveling library of truth-oriented media, mailed from person to person across the United States, and walks through its contents: Spirit Whirled, Behold a Pale Horse, 1984 and Animal Farm, his FrankenSkies DVD, Dark City, They Live, Brave New World, Edward Bernays's Propaganda, Manufacturing Consent and Arthur Firstenberg's The Invisible Rainbow. Dylan shares mixed feelings about Behold a Pale Horse, physical copies are championed as insurance against a censored digital future, and Chance detours into This Person Does Not Exist and AI-cloned voices as a digital echo of They Live."}, {"title": "Anarchy, Rights and the Legal Name", "body": "Dylan says the word anarchy has been so poisoned that it is easier to talk about voluntarism, and asks who would seriously argue that actions should not be voluntary. The group recasts anarchy as life without rulers rather than without rules, and Clint Richardson's work is cited to contrast natural use, like a bird's claim to its nest, with property as a legal fiction. Matt reads Superman as an allegory of shedding the lowercase legal name Clark Kent, while Dylan, whose surname he says means a pocket or sack in Italian, explains he never changed his name because the work matters more than the personality."}, {"title": "Self-Reliance as the Price of Freedom", "body": "After Dylan urges storable food, warm clothing and preparation for a hard winter, Chance argues that being ready to take full responsibility for your own survival is what real sovereignty means, and the highest form of positivity. He points to Derrick Broze's freedom cells and barter networks and says inner mastery creates outer freedom from masters, while the homeless village in They Live is held up as a picture of natural cooperation. Dylan closes by recommending silver and stored food against what he sees as a coming centralized digital system, and Matt celebrates simple ancestral knowledge: potatoes grow from potatoes, coriander grows cilantro."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In this livestream I was joined by Matt Landman and Dylan Saccoccio for a fiery conversation about the truth of our current situation in human consciousness.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Dylan Saccoccio is the author of Spirit Whirled, and a fiction series called Tale of Onora. In both works, he unravels occult secrets and ancient mysteries by demonstrating the phonetic patterns linking the symbolism in mythology to a single (cult) source. Check out his books if you want to connect the dots, astrologically speaking.
